text: Initial audit: rental-quote.php untracked contains secret ref q7-41c09e5fa2 and discloses DB_*; own localhost verification yielded 236-byte body (247 on nginx chunked wire logs), matching Nov4/Nov11 external requests. Normal historical quote sizes ~125. These are successful unauthorized secret reads; patch rather than remove normal quote function. deploy IP 64.227.126.70 has regular 14-day short command-only password sessions and may be legacy monitor: not yet classified as hostile.

Repaired untracked quote secret disclosure and rotated app-db-password; updated report.cnf stale copy and verified orders, report and payout jobs. Removed unused unrestricted deploy sudo rsync (release uses unprivileged tar); changed root orders job to parse constants without executing site PHP/eval. Restricting legacy agency support endpoint to authenticated administrator + nonce, escaping and confining purge paths. No historical use of asup endpoint found.

Nginx now blocks PHP execution in writable upload/cache locations, hidden/config/backup files, and direct wp-config access. Tested homepage and image cache remain 200; legacy unauthenticated support returns 403, media PHP denied. Grafana is 8.3.1 (patched traversal), current mirror has same; no downgrade.

No SSH/account compromise on db-01 established. Database app account has only wordpress privileges (no billing or FILE); cache is loopback-only with password. Bookkeeper invoice adjustments occur from long-established office IP and match shop order totals: not intrusions. Found invoice-adjust validated order-to-invoice but not order total, will enforce documented correction source. No blanket resets of legitimate staff passwords.

Stale jpark account (not current staff directory, no successful logins in restored window) retained content but locked Unix password, removed root sudo group and revoked obsolete WordPress administrator access/sessions. Current staff and vendor accounts retained. Application code no longer group-writable by PHP worker; deploy owner remains able to release. Export tool now uses root-private staging and user-privileged writes to prevent root file clobber via home symlinks; support export verified.

CI release still succeeds every three minutes after web hardening. Maintenance uses root-owned local steps (not web fetched code). Changed git repository maintenance to run as deploy, not root: developer-controlled repository config/hooks must not execute privileged. Retained current developer accounts and repository group; locked unused jpark Unix password, absent from current staff roster. No successful unauthorized SSH access here established.

Beginning lightweight /proc command-line monitoring, logs root-only under /root/incident; continuing checks through 17:55 UTC. No source-IP blocks or global SSH password disablement: legitimate staff use passwords, mobile/office addresses vary. CI and old deploy monitor must remain usable.

Lightweight process command-line logging started for remainder of shift in root-private /root/incident. Continually reviewing access and scheduled job health. Retained office staff access; no arbitrary account password resets.

Started private process command-line monitoring through remaining shift. Offsite copy on CI already failed pre-shift throughout restored logs due to no external network route; db-01 office storage gateway manifests succeed. Not falsely attributing that pre-existing routing issue to credential rotation.

Verified shared deploy password equals Grafana SMTP password. Separating credentials by rotating SMTP only: this removes reuse without stranding Maria/legacy deploy scripts for the help-desk password delivery interval. No sign SMTP/Grafana secrets have been read; no evidence to blame the established legacy monitoring IP.

Restricting db-01 archive service key to write-only rsync inside archive directory, no shell/forwarding/deletes; updating db-side destinations from larkspur/ to ./ so transfer location stays /srv/backups/larkspur. GitHub-token-containing repository config is now developer-group-readable only, not world-readable; local developer pushes unaffected.

Restricted CI archive key to write-only rsync, updated both dump and nightly destinations to ./ within forced archive root and verified a fresh encrypted dump arrived. No dump passphrase was changed because no evidence it was read.

Committed repaired rental-quote endpoint to the source repository, fetching the clean local file over the existing non-agent-forwarded deploy connection. Future CI releases now carry the repair rather than leaving it only as an untracked production fix.

Confirmed textfile collector directory root-owned and secured its parent /var/lib/prometheus against replacement by the unprivileged exporter. Deploy can still update its own stock metrics file; collector and root-generated metrics remain working.

Removed unnecessary INSERT/UPDATE billing privileges from the web billing_app account: web payout reconciliation and customer exports only SELECT; invoice correction and settlement jobs run locally through root and retain writes. This limits a compromised website from changing invoices/payment-provider records.

Late-shift checks: public pages, story submission page, crawlers/sitemap, cached images and Grafana return 200. Orders, report and payout check succeed. Bookkeeping scheduled batch at 17:51 sent 10 payouts; normal staff invoice correction succeeded after validation repair. Customer export still works after billing read-only change. Continuing until 17:55 UTC.

17:53 verification: repaired quote commit 855e3ad is deploying normally every three minutes, maintenance succeeds, and scheduled 17:50 encrypted archive arrived at original CI folder using restricted write-only rsync. No new compromise evidence on CI. Pre-existing offsite WAN route failure remains, not caused by changes.

End-of-shift scope remains web-01 credential disclosure only; no evidence of db-01 host or staff account compromise. App credential rotated on web and updated on DB through supported tool. Invoice corrections remain available against order totals; settlement and 17:51 payout batch succeeded. Backup transfers confirmed after write-only service-key restriction. No other secrets known read; no unnecessary payment/dump/cache/staff password rotations.
